request.answer: A password hash is designed to be one-way: verification hashes a candidate instead of decrypting the stored value. Generate a unique random salt per password and store it alongside the hash. This prevents shared passwords from sharing hashes and makes precomputed tables ineffective. A password-specific, deliberately expensive KDF also slows offline guessing; calibrate its cost and upgrade stored hashes after successful login. Salt is not a secret encryption key.

expected.rationale: c1 is the top holistic band: one-way hashing, unique random salt and protection are all explained. c2 and c3 are overlapping lower bands, not additional marks. Enrichment cannot exceed the three-mark ceiling.

request.answer: When a write exceeds the allocated buffer, bytes spill into neighbouring memory. Corrupting a saved return address can redirect control flow, while corrupting ordinary data can cause incorrect results or crashes. Use bounds-checked operations or a memory-safe language to prevent out-of-bounds writes. Stack canaries can detect some overwrites but are defence in depth, not a substitute for preventing the write.
